# Kitsu / Zou external API client — Sprint 382, Story 354

The client connects only to a caller-configured, user-managed Zou service. It does not install, start, download, embed, or manage a Kitsu/Zou server. Validation here uses loopback HTTP fixtures; real-account validation belongs to Sprint 465. The implementation uses only Go standard-library HTTP code and does not copy Zou source.

## Contract and limits

A caller supplies a scoped bearer token for network operations. A tokenless client can produce dry-run effects; reads and executions return `ErrMissingCredential` without network access. The client keeps a supplied token only in memory, sends it in the Authorization header, and never puts it in effects or errors. Remote base URLs require HTTPS; plaintext HTTP is allowed only for loopback fixtures. Invalid UUID path arguments, unknown read operations, and unsupported review actions fail before any request. The copied HTTP client applies a same-origin redirect policy even when a client is injected. Every request has a maximum 15-second context deadline and responses are capped at 4 MiB.

Both writes, `DeleteComment` and `CreateComment`, require exactly one explicit `WithDryRun()` or `WithExecute()` option. Zero or conflicting options return `ErrExecutionNotExplicit`. Dry-run returns an effect without network access. `CreateComment` sends only `task_status_id` and `comment` as JSON; its effect summarizes the status ID and comment byte count without retaining the comment text. It limits comment text to 16 KiB and the encoded request to 20 KiB. Zou's handler changes task status as part of comment creation. A valid JSON 201 marks a created comment executed; a successful 204 marks a deleted comment executed.

The source inspected did not justify generic `/data/versions` or `/data/reviews` routes, generic review mutations, or generic project/episode/sequence/shot/task mutation payloads. They are absent or return typed `ErrUnsupported`; no route is guessed. Reads return bounded JSON so callers can decode shapes according to their Zou deployment version. Project task pagination is server-defined; a caller can request a particular `page` but this client does not claim to retrieve all pages automatically.

## Verification

`go test ./external/kitsu` and `go vet ./external/kitsu` pass against in-process fixtures. Tests cover every allowlisted path, query encoding, token header, loopback/HTTPS validation, cross-origin redirects with an injected client, invalid operations and IDs, response bound, timeout, explicit write modes, dry-run zero calls, POST path/body/header, oversize rejection, executed 201, and executed 204.
